title: Scalar energy-weighted Q3 slice bound
question: Does the candidate energy A(q)=1+q^4 absorb the cubic growth of the actual Q3 slice with an exact finite coefficient majorant?
method: Reconstruct the EXP-001052 source slice v=0, a=1/4 in primary SymPy and independent Fraction arithmetic.
Compute the exact coefficient triangle C=59139/35840 and verify the all-real power-majorant conditions for degrees 0 through 3, with exact fourth-power sample self-tests at q=0,1,2,4,8,32.
Compile Lean R235 for the coefficient-majorant identity, positivity, exponent and degree fixtures while preserving the scalar-only scope firewall.
finding: For P_0(q)=(51/140)q^3-(153/1120)q^2+(2291/2240)q-4531/35840 and A(q)=1+q^4, the coefficient triangle gives the exact all-real scalar bound |P_0(q)| <= (59139/35840) A(q)^(3/4). Both arithmetic lanes and Lean R235 reproduce the constant and exact sample inequalities. This is a scalar weighted interface only.
decision_reason: This is the first positive follow-up to the EXP-001052 ordinary-norm boundary: the candidate energy weight matches the cubic source growth at an exact scalar level. It selects a plausible QFT domain seminorm without silently promoting it to the multivariate Q3 operator or history theorem.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing scalar weighted interface. It does not establish the actual Q3 common core, operator domain closure, multivariate source estimate, factorial incidence, or thermodynamic QFT.
